briefs.text: Tehran rules out any talks with Washington until its seven conditions are met.
A car bomb destroys buildings in Villavicencio; no confirmed victims, the president says.
Bitcoin slips below $60,000 as US spot bitcoin ETFs suffer record monthly outflows of about $4.7bn.
Landmine casualties hit a five-year high of about 7,000, Myanmar and Syria worst affected.

cards.body: The United Kingdom, Spain, Canada, Australia and ten other countries affirmed the International Court of Justice decision that Myanmar's military committed genocide against the Rohingya minority.
cards.headline: Fourteen nations back ICJ ruling of Rohingya genocide

cards.body: President Zelenskyy confirmed Ukraine struck a Russian vessel in the Gulf of Finland. Kyiv also said a Russian air strike on Zaporizhzhia killed two people and wounded more than 40.
cards.headline: Ukraine strikes Russian vessel in Gulf of Finland

cards.body: Brussels proposed a 22nd package of sanctions over the invasion of Ukraine, this time targeting Russia's banks, soldiers and athletes.
cards.headline: EU unveils 22nd sanctions package against Russia

cards.body: UN secretary-general Antonio Guterres urged member states to agree, within the next year, a multilateral framework for managing the risks of artificial intelligence.
cards.headline: Guterres seeks global AI guardrails within a year

cards.body: The Dow rose 0.85% to 50,018.70, its first close above 50,000, even as the Nasdaq fell 1.48%: Nvidia slid 5.86%, the chip index lost 7.88%, and Anthropic dropped below its $83 IPO price.
cards.headline: Dow closes above 50,000 as AI sell-off deepens

cards.body: A magnitude 5.6 earthquake struck Koshi province in eastern Nepal, close to the border with China. There were no immediate reports of casualties.
cards.headline: Magnitude 5.6 quake rattles Nepal near China border

footer: Compiled from agency reports — AFP · AP · Reuters · Dawn · Interfax · SCMP · CoinDesk

lead.body: A Houthi drone struck the 80-storey PIF Tower in Riyadh's financial district on Tuesday, the second hit on Saudi Arabia's tallest skyscraper in under a week. Saudi Civil Defence said 11 people were injured; the Saudi-led coalition condemned the strike as a terrorist attack.
lead.headline: Houthi drone hits Riyadh's tallest tower a second time

tagline: One day of world news, in one picture
